comparison.giva: Bodies not returned, so length was not measured. Headlines run 3-9 words (catalogue headlines are six card titles joined by pipes). The keyword matches suggest long bodies: most of the 14 sampled ads match three to six separate claims (code, lifetime, warranty, returns, certified, free shipping). That is an inference, not a measurement.
comparison.palmonas: Bodies not returned. The only measured figure is from the 19 Aug 2026 Motion pull (docs/research/01-competitor-corpus.md): median caption 279 characters. Headlines are pipe-joined offer strings, and the catalogue headlines carry six price and name cards.
comparison.naira: Measured. ads-20: median 129 characters (115-157), 26 words, one paragraph. toggle-15: median 149 (132-200). Manifest: median 272.5 characters (233-327), 51 words, in two paragraphs split by a blank line. The 15 sampled here run 250-308.
comparison.verdict: Naira's ads-20 length is right: the hook, the fact and most of the offer show before '...more' (about 125 characters in Feed). The manifest's 270 characters, like Palmonas's 279, hide the offer and proof behind '...more'. For Shop All, write 120-180 characters in one paragraph.

comparison.giva: Headlines lead with the brand, the occasion or the offer: 'Giva Now Delivers in Just', 'Shubh Dhanteras is 2 hours', 'Celebrate Traditions with Pure Silver', 'Flat 20% Off ₹999+ |', 'Bring Out Your Inner Pataka!'. The body openings were not visible.
comparison.palmonas: Number or offer first: '1000+ Pieces starting at ₹999', 'Buy 4 at ₹2,999 |', 'EXTRA 40% OFF | The', 'Buy 9KT on Dhanteras this', and '₹999 | Cute Heart Bracelet' on the catalogue cards.
comparison.naira: The manifest opens with a familiar thing, turned, in 2-5 words: 'Finer than pheni.', 'Choodi, for your ears.', 'A ladi that never fuses.', 'Ghungroo, on mute.', 'Rangoli you can wear.'. Some are generic ('Date night.', 'Dress code: sparkle.', 'Make an entrance.'). ads-20 mostly opens with plain description ('A fine line of red', 'A braided rope of gold', 'Oval links and a toggle') or with the offer ('Pick any three and take'). The set-2 openings ('Greener than the mehendi:', 'The gajra's plus-one:') follow the winning grammar.
comparison.verdict: Naira wins, but only when the first five words name an Indian thing and turn it. That is the grammar behind 'Rangoli, in a line.' (6.10%), 'Anaar, pre-peeled.' (5.49%) and 'Finer than pheni.' (4.32%). ads-20's description-first openings waste the hook. Do not copy the competitors' brand-first or percent-first openings: the brief says discount hooks are saturated in India.

comparison.giva: The offer is in the headline ('Flat 20% Off ₹999+ | Code: BLING', 'Buy 2 Get 15% Off | New Customer Exclusive'). 'code' matches about 242 of about 434 active ads. Codes are the house default: in the Aug pull, a code appeared in 105 of 151 creatives and 80% of copy carried an offer.
comparison.palmonas: The offer is the headline. 'The Diwali Sale' matches about 1,255 of about 2,158 active ads, alongside 'Buy 4 at ₹2,999', 'EXTRA 40% OFF' and 'FLAT 50% OFF on Diwali Gift boxes'. 'code' matches about 96. In the Aug pull, 58% of copy carried an offer and 23% used urgency.
comparison.naira: The offer comes last. In ads-20 it starts at 53-77% of the way through the caption. The exception is the five set-3 'reason to buy' ads (S3_11 to S3_15), which open with the offer or a service fact. In the manifest the offer sits alone in a second paragraph and still says 'with codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout', which is stale: the bag now applies it.
comparison.verdict: Naira's placement is correct for the brief (offer low in the hierarchy, or as the twist). The wording has to be fixed: 'Buy 2, get 10% off. Buy 3, get 20% off, applied in your bag.' No codes, no 'sale', no percent-off against a compare-at price.

comparison.dimension: Proof / trust lines (shipping, COD, returns, warranty, ratings)
comparison.giva: The densest stack. Approximate matches across about 434 active ads: lifetime 237, returns 218, warranty 201, '925 silver warranty' 137, certified 134, free shipping 123, hypoallergenic 103, cash on delivery 1. It also sells speed ('Giva Now Delivers in Just 2 Hours'). Ratings were not tested.
comparison.palmonas: Material claims rather than service proof: demifine 373, waterproof 62, 18k 55, 'waterproof anti-tarnish' 49, returns 16, lifetime 5, free shipping 0, COD 0. Physical stores appear as proof ('📍 Visit PALMONAS Store at Turner Road!').
comparison.naira: True, specific service facts: free insured shipping, 3-5 working days, COD on serviceable pincodes, the Naira gift box, adjustable US 5-9. But each ads-20 caption carries at most one, and most carry only the offer. 7-day returns appears in none of the 45 captions. The manifest says 'cash on delivery across India', which overclaims: COD covers serviceable pincodes only.
comparison.verdict: GIVA wins on volume and Naira wins on truth. A cold Shop All audience needs one short service line per caption, rotated across the 10 ads: free insured shipping in 3-5 working days, 7-day returns, COD on serviceable pincodes, the gift box. Never borrow the durability claims (waterproof, anti-tarnish, hypoallergenic): they are banned for Naira.

comparison.giva: Emoji and exclamation marks in headlines ('Bring Out Your Inner Pataka! 🪔'), Title Case throughout, pipes. One live collection ad shows the raw placeholder 'default_collection_headline'. Body emoji could not be seen.
comparison.palmonas: ALL-CAPS offers ('EXTRA 40% OFF', 'FLAT 50% OFF', 'PALMONAS'), the 🪔 and 📍 emoji, '!', and pipe-stacked price and name strings.
comparison.naira: No emoji in any caption. No '!' in ads-20 or toggle-15, and one in the manifest ('Kai po che!'). Sentence case. The manifest splits each caption into two paragraphs with a blank line; ads-20 and toggle-15 are single paragraphs. Headlines use '·'.
comparison.verdict: Naira's restraint is on brand and stands out in a feed full of 🪔 and caps. Keep zero emoji and zero '!' (remove 'Kai po che!'), and keep one paragraph.

comparison.giva: The button was not returned by the tool. Headlines are brand-centred invitations ('Find your festive favourite at GIVA', 'Celebrate with Giva'). The same page also runs a franchise lead ad ('Own a GIVA Store').
comparison.palmonas: The button was not returned. Headlines are imperative: 'Buy 9KT on Dhanteras', 'Buy 4 at ₹2,999', 'Visit PALMONAS Store', 'Unwrap Gifts From PALMONAS'.
comparison.naira: Shop now on every ad (captions.json; manifest cta SHOP_NOW). The text never says 'shop now' and ends on the offer or a fact. Headline: product · price.
comparison.verdict: Even on the button, since everyone uses Shop now. Naira should keep the command out of the text. For Shop All, the headline changes job: it should carry the range and the entry price ('130+ pieces, from ₹599'), not one product's name.

comparison.giva: Festive, brand-centred clichés ('Make This Diwali Truly Meaningful', 'Celebrate Traditions with Pure Silver', 'Shine Like a Pataka'). One sharp line: 'Shubh Dhanteras is 2 hours away' ties the festival to the 2-hour delivery.
comparison.palmonas: A sale machine: one named sale, numbers and caps, repeated across more than a thousand ads. Little voice beyond 'Unwrap Gifts'.
comparison.naira: A sharp, wry friend who is exact: 'Ghungroo, on mute.', 'Mummy's bow, minus the tug.', 'Three colours, zero outfit drama'. It drifts in the generic occasion lines ('Date night.', 'Dress code: sparkle.', 'Make an entrance.'), the kind the brief's own data puts under 2.2% CTR.
comparison.verdict: Naira clearly wins. Cut every line that could sell anything.

comparison.giva: Material and service facts ('Pure Silver'; 925, silver and warranty together in about 137 ads; '2 Hours'). Product names appear only as catalogue card titles ('Silver Mystic Moonbeam Link Chain'). No sizes visible.
comparison.palmonas: A price on every catalogue card ('₹2,580 | Emerald Aventurine Necklace'). Range plus price floor ('1000+ pieces starting at ₹999'). No sizes visible.
comparison.naira: The most specific of the three: mm, cm, cut, colour, setting, tone and exact price with the Indian comma ('15mm gold tone huggies with one row of baguettes', '50 cm of 4 mm paperclip links'). Faults in the manifest: '18k gold tone' and 'rhodium silver tone' where the brief says plain 'gold tone' and 'silver tone', and 'tiger's eye' (a gem name) in the Halo Curve captions. Spacing is inconsistent ('15mm' vs '15 mm').
comparison.verdict: Naira wins. Palmonas's range-plus-floor line is the one structure worth taking for Shop All, written Naira's way and true: '130+ pieces from ₹599', the four categories, then one named piece with its pool.json price and one exact detail.

comparison.giva: Light festive loanwords inside English headlines: 'Pataka' ('Bring Out Your Inner Pataka!', 'Shine Like a Pataka'), 'Shubh Dhanteras'.
comparison.palmonas: None in the headlines beyond festival names (Diwali, Dhanteras).
comparison.naira: Hindi nouns and short phrases that carry the hook: 'Kabhi front, kabhi side', 'Kaagaz ki kashti', choodi, ladi, ghungroo, kesar, pheni, mehendi, gajra, sangeet, haldi, Banarasi; also Gujarati 'Kai po che!'. No full Hinglish sentences. The 'hook laga do' idea survived only in the file name: the caption itself is English.
comparison.verdict: Naira uses it best: one Hindi word or 3-4 word phrase that lands the hook, with the rest in plain English. Keep that dose.

rules: 1. Length and shape: one paragraph, 120-180 characters, no line breaks. The hook and the range fact must sit inside the first 125 characters so they show before '...more'. Model: 'Rangoli, in a line. One of 130+ pieces from ₹599: the Prism Rivière Bracelet, silver tone, ₹2,399. Buy 2, get 10% off. Buy 3, get 20% off, applied in your bag.' (159 characters)

2. First 2-5 words: name one familiar Indian thing that is really in the photo (rangoli, anaar, pheni, mishri, elaichi, potli, toran, a saree pallu) and turn it, or state a craft truth as 'X, not Y' ('Woven, not cast.'). Never open with a percentage, a price, the brand name, 'Shop', 'Celebrate' or 'Discover', or an occasion that could sell anything ('Date night.', 'Dress code: sparkle.').

3. Sell the range in the next clause: '130+ pieces from ₹599' (never 135, never a rounded-up boast). Add the four categories when there is room: rings, earrings, necklaces, bracelets. For a pool hero you may say 'our most-clicked pieces', and nowhere else.

4. Name the piece shown, with its exact pool.json price (₹ sign, Indian comma: ₹1,199) and one exact detail (25 mm, ruby red, adjustable US 5 to 9). The photo earns the stop; the caption proves the stop was worth it.

5. The offer goes last, in these words: 'Buy 2, get 10% off. Buy 3, get 20% off, applied in your bag.' No codes (drop BUY2/BUY3), no 'sale', no percent-off against compare-at prices, and never the offer in the first five words.

6. Add one proof line, rotated across the 10 ads: 'Free insured shipping, 3-5 working days.' / '7-day returns.' / 'Cash on delivery on serviceable pincodes.' (never 'across India') / 'Every piece arrives in the Naira gift box.' At most two per caption. No ratings, order counts or reviews.

7. Material words: 'gold tone' and 'silver tone' only (drop '18k' and 'rhodium'); 'cubic zirconia' or the colour (ruby red, emerald green, aqua); 'shell pearl'; no gem names (tiger's eye, emerald or ruby as nouns). Never: real, diamond, gold, silver, waterproof, tarnish words, hypoallergenic, stunning, elevate, must-have, luxury.

8. Formatting: sentence case, full stops, no emoji, no exclamation marks, no hashtags, no pipes, no ALL CAPS except one short word at most. The quiet caption is the differentiator in a feed of 🪔 and 'FLAT 50% OFF'.
9. Hinglish dose: at most one Hindi word or short phrase, used as or inside the hook, that an urban reader needs no gloss for (kabhi, potli, choodi, ladi, ghungroo). Everything else in plain English.
10. No urgency or scarcity of any kind: no countdowns, 'limited time', 'only X left', 'hurry' or festival deadlines, even where stock is genuinely low (the Ruby huggies have 4 units).

11. CTA and headline: leave 'Shop now' to Meta's button and keep it out of the text. Headline at most 40 characters, carrying the range and the entry price ('130+ pieces, from ₹599' or 'All pieces · from ₹599'). Link to https://nairaflore.com/jewellery.
12. The transfer test: if the caption would still work under a different photo or another brand's ad, rewrite it. Never name or allude to a competitor, and never compare.

scores.why: GIVA and Palmonas are scored provisionally: their primary texts could not be read, so their scores rest on verbatim live headlines, keyword-match counts across their active ads and the 19 Aug 2026 corpus. GIVA 6: the strongest trust stack in the category (lifetime, warranty, returns, certified and free shipping each in roughly 30-55% of active ads) and one clever line ('Shubh Dhanteras is 2 hours away'). Against that: code-led offers (BLING), brand-centred festive clichés, emoji and Title Case, and a live 'default_collection_headline' placeholder. Palmonas 5: one message ('The Diwali Sale') stamped on over a thousand ads, percent and price first, caps and emoji, no service proof (0 free shipping, 0 COD) and durability claims (waterproof, anti-tarnish). Its 'range plus price floor' line and price-per-card catalogue titles are clear, and are the one structure worth taking. Naira 7.5 (ads-20 7.5, toggle-15 8, manifest 6.5 as written today): the best hooks, voice and product specificity, with no emoji, caps or code-speak. It loses points because the 110-caption manifest still says 'codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout' and 'cash on delivery across India', uses '18k', 'rhodium' and 'tiger's eye', has one 'Kai po che!' and identical boilerplate behind '...more' at about 270 characters. ads-20 often wastes the first five words on description. Generic occasion hooks recur, 7-day returns is never mentioned, and no caption yet sells the range.
